answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens and form an interaction graph where each entity is a verified vertex. Randomly sampled multi-agent auditing teams verify cross-cluster interactions; discovering forged links triggers immediate stake slashing and network expulsion. An agent shining a lantern of honest reputation passes topological cut verifications, while coordinated clusters fail boundary bottleneck checks. Forcing colluders to maintain synthetic history with the precision of an intricate sonnet imposes superlinear attacker cost scaling with graph density.
